requirement_text: A*AA including A* in Mathematics, and a minimum of one science subject from the following list: Computer Science, Further Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, or Physics.
researcher_notes: A-level typical offer. Page is the 2027-entry course page, explicitly titled '(2027 entry)'. Manchester is the highest-programme-count institution in ORYN's corpus (294 programmes) and had zero requirement rows before this batch.

requirement_text: The mathematics A-Level must include a significant pure element.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary: only the phrase 'a significant pure element' survived the extraction step as a quotation. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: Paired with the exclusion in REQ-2026-08-21-9003, which names the two maths qualifications that do NOT satisfy this.

requirement_text: Use of Mathematics or Core Mathematics do not satisfy this requirement.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION. A student holding A-level 'Use of Mathematics' at A* meets REQ-9001's letter grade and is nonetheless disqualified. Stored beside the positive rule without is_exclusion this would read as a second way to qualify.

requirement_text: Science A-Levels require passing the practical component.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: A grade alone does not evidence this; the practical endorsement is a separate fact ORYN does not currently store.

requirement_text: 37 points overall with 7,6,6 in Higher Level subjects, including 7 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches.
researcher_notes: IB Diploma. Recorded on the IB scale. No conversion to or from A-level letters or any GPA.

requirement_text: a minimum of one science subject at Higher Level
researcher_notes: Page enumerates the accepted science subjects as Computer Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biology.

requirement_text: Only Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches meets the mathematics requirement.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION by implication: IB HL Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at 7 does NOT satisfy REQ-9005 despite being HL maths at the stated grade. This is the single most common IB mis-evaluation and a bare scalar cannot express it.

requirement_text: minimum of five GCSEs/IGCSEs, including GCSE Mathematics at grade B/6, GCSE English Language at grade B/6, and three further academic subjects at grade C/4.
researcher_notes: GCSE grades on the UK 9-1 / A*-G scales as published. No conversion.

requirement_text: English Literature and English as a Second Language are not accepted.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION against REQ-9008's 'GCSE English Language at grade B/6'. Directly affects international applicants, who commonly hold IGCSE English as a Second Language.

requirement_text: IELTS 7.0 overall, with no subscore below 6.5
researcher_notes: IELTS 0-9 band scale, unchanged by the 2026 ETS rescale. Unambiguous.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT 100 overall, with no subscore below 22
limitations: TOEFL SCALE DEFECT, same shape as Glasgow and Bogazici in requirements_batch5_scale-audit. The 2027-entry page carries no scale qualifier and no cutover date. 100/22 is unambiguously the pre-21-January-2026 0-120 and 0-30 scales. The '100 overall' half remains meetable because ETS supplies a comparable 0-120 overall on score reports until January 2028; the 'no subscore below 22' half is NOT meetable by any report issued after 21 January 2026, because ETS reports sections on the 1-6 scale and does not restate them on 0-30. A naive comparison would tell a 2027-entry applicant they FAILED an unmeasurable requirement. Must evaluate to needs_manual_review until Manchester republishes.
researcher_notes: This is a 2027-entry page, i.e. it governs applicants sitting TOEFL entirely after the cutover, which makes the defect materially worse than on a 2026-entry page. Contrast Exeter (REQ-9024/9025), Bath (REQ-9018/9019) and Liverpool, which all publish both scales explicitly.

requirement_text: GCSE/IGCSE English Language grade B/6
researcher_notes: Listed as one of the alternative routes to the English requirement, alongside IELTS and TOEFL. Subject to the REQ-9009 exclusion.

requirement_text: T Levels are not accepted.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION at qualification-type level. T Levels are an England-only qualification, hence applies_to domestic.

requirement_text: The BTEC National Certificate is not considered for entry.
limitations: text_fidelity is extracted_summary. Re-read the source before showing this string to a student. The page distinguishes BTEC sizes (Certificate vs Extended Diploma); only the Certificate was captured as excluded, so the treatment of larger BTECs is unrecorded here rather than known-absent.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION at qualification-size level.

requirement_text: usually the equivalent of IELTS 6.0-7.0 (or 5.5 for foundation courses)
limitations: NOT A THRESHOLD. This is a range across the whole institution, hedged with 'usually' and 'equivalent'. It cannot be evaluated: a student at IELTS 6.5 is above the bottom and below the top of the same rule. Recorded so the next lane does not re-derive it and mistake it for a university-wide minimum. The page itself says 'The minimum English language requirements for each programme are specified on individual course profiles.'
researcher_notes: Manchester publishes NO evaluable university-wide English threshold. For all 294 Manchester programmes the requirement lives only on the per-course page, which is why REQ-9010/9011 had to be sourced at course level. This is the coverage-shape finding for Manchester, not a usable rule.

requirement_text: A*AA in three A levels.
limitations: This is the September 2026 entry page, retrieved 2026-08-21. The 2026 cycle has closed. Bath's 2027-entry course pages were not confirmed to exist at retrieval time; do not assume this offer carries forward.
researcher_notes: Labelled 'typical offer' by the page, distinct from the contextual offer in REQ-9017.

requirement_text: AAB in three A levels.
limitations: CONTEXTUAL OFFER. Only available to applicants who meet Bath's separate widening-participation eligibility criteria, which this row does not carry. Evaluating a student against this number without checking that eligibility would tell an ineligible student they qualify at AAB when the rule for them is A*AA.
researcher_notes: Recorded deliberately: a requirement store that holds only the typical offer misrepresents UK admissions, but a store that holds the contextual offer WITHOUT its eligibility gate is worse. This is a second shape a scalar threshold cannot carry - a conditional applicability predicate on the rule itself.

requirement_text: 36 points overall and 7, 6, 6 in three Higher Level subjects.
limitations: September 2026 entry page. Cycle closed.
researcher_notes: IB typical offer. Recorded on the IB scale.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (taken up to 21 January 2026): 100 overall with a minimum 24 in all 4 components
limitations: Bounded to tests taken up to 21 January 2026, so it is unambiguous on its own terms and NOT subject to the Glasgow/Manchester subtest defect. It does, however, become unmeetable in January 2028 when ETS stops supplying comparable 0-120 scores.
researcher_notes: EXEMPLARY SOURCE. Bath states the cutover date explicitly and publishes both scales as separate rows. Compare Manchester REQ-9011, which publishes one undated number for 2027 entry. Bath's own central Category A page (REQ-9021) does NOT carry this qualifier - within one institution, the course page is the safer source.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (taken after 21 January 2026): 5 overall with a minimum 4.5 in all components
researcher_notes: The post-cutover 1-6 band scale, correctly applied: 5 overall is within ETS's stated 1-6 range and the subtest floor of 4.5 is expressible on the scale ETS now reports. This is what a correctly-migrated TOEFL requirement looks like, and is the counter-example that proves Manchester's and Glasgow's rows are defects rather than an unavoidable state of the world.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT and iBT Home Edition: 100 overall with 24 in each component
limitations: No cutover date or scale qualifier survived extraction from this central page, although Bath's own course pages (REQ-9019/9020) split the same Category A requirement into two dated rows. Either the central page genuinely omits the qualifier, or the extraction dropped a row. Not safe to ingest as a standalone threshold either way. Prefer the course-level rows.
researcher_notes: Bath groups all courses into English categories A/B/C; this page is the university-wide definition of Category A. Recorded because the grouping itself is reusable structure - one Bath category row can serve many programmes once the course-to-category mapping is known.

requirement_text: IELTS Academic and IELTS Online: 7.0 with 6.5 in each component
researcher_notes: IELTS 0-9, unaffected by the ETS rescale.

requirement_text: Cambridge C1 Advanced & C2 Proficiency: 185 with no less than 176 in all elements
researcher_notes: Cambridge English Scale, unchanged. Unambiguous.

requirement_text: We do not accept the PTE Academic online test
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION on test DELIVERY MODE, not on score. A student with PTE Academic 69 taken online holds a numerically qualifying score Bath rejects. Same shape as Edinburgh's IELTS One Skill Retake and Koc's superscore exclusions. Note Bath accepts 'IELTS Online' (REQ-9022) but not 'PTE Academic online' - the online/in-centre distinction is per test, not a general policy, so it cannot be generalised.

requirement_text: no more than 24 months before starting your course
limitations: RECENCY RULE, the shape documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md section 2. Anchor is 'starting your course', not the application date - a different anchor from Edinburgh's 'prior to entry'. A student meeting the score with a 30-month-old certificate is currently told they qualify.
researcher_notes: Applies to the English tests, not to school qualifications. Must force needs_manual_review on every Bath English row until qualification age is modelled.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (from January 21, 2026): Overall score 5.0 with a minimum score of 4.5 in writing and no less than 4.0 in all other sections
researcher_notes: Post-cutover 1-6 scale, correctly applied with a per-section floor that is expressible on the scale ETS actually reports. Second exemplary source after Bath.

requirement_text: 100 with minimum scores of 25 for writing, and no less than 21 for listening, reading and speaking.
limitations: The legacy 0-120/0-30 row. Unambiguous ONLY because Exeter publishes it as a separate row from the post-21-January-2026 row (REQ-9026); read alone it would look like Manchester's undated defect. Becomes unmeetable January 2028 when ETS ends comparable 0-120 reporting.
researcher_notes: Listed by Exeter as the standard TOEFL iBT row, sitting immediately above the from-January-2026 row.

requirement_text: Overall score 7.0 with a minimum score of 6.5 in writing and no less than 6.0 in all other sections
researcher_notes: IELTS Academic and Academic variants. Per-section floors differ between writing and the other three - a single scalar 'minimum band' cannot express this row.

requirement_text: 70 with no less than 67 in writing skills and 64 in all other communicative skills
researcher_notes: Pearson PTE Academic.

requirement_text: Botswana General Certificate of Secondary Education (BTGCSE) Not accepted
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION by named qualification. Sits inside a table whose other rows are acceptances, which is precisely the storage hazard: dropped into the same list without is_exclusion it reads as a qualifying route.

requirement_text: Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education Not accepted
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION by named qualification, same table as REQ-9030.

requirement_text: Tests valid for 2 years
limitations: RECENCY RULE. Exeter splits its table into a '2 years' group (the tests) and a '7 years' group (school qualifications such as A/AS level English Language grade C and GCSE English Language grade B/6), so the validity window differs BY QUALIFICATION TYPE within one profile. A single per-institution max-age field cannot represent this.
researcher_notes: Same finding shape as Koc (tests 2 years, diplomas unlimited) and Edinburgh (2 years for some tests, 3.5 for others, none for majority-English nationals). Three institutions in three countries all carry per-qualification-type validity windows; this is a general rule, not an outlier.

requirement_text: IELTS 6.0 overall, with no component less than 5.5, or equivalent
limitations: This is the institution-wide FLOOR, not the requirement for any particular programme. Liverpool's page states clinical programmes require up to IELTS 7.5. Evaluating a Medicine applicant against 6.0 would return met when the real rule is 7.0+.
researcher_notes: Recorded as a floor with that limitation attached rather than as a programme requirement.

requirement_text: IELTS 7.0 overall, with no component less than 6.5, or equivalent
limitations: The page lists three IELTS bands (6.0/5.5, 6.5/5.5, 7.0/6.5) but the mapping of band to programme did not survive extraction intact. Do not attach this to a named programme without re-reading the source.
researcher_notes: Recorded at medium confidence with the mapping explicitly unresolved rather than guessed.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (excluding TOEFL Home Edition which is not accepted)
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION on test delivery mode, and it points the OPPOSITE WAY from Bath, which accepts 'TOEFL iBT and iBT Home Edition' (REQ-9021). Two UK universities, same test, opposite home-edition policies. Any shared 'accepted tests' lookup that is not per-institution will be wrong for one of them.

requirement_text: IELTS certificates are valid for two years. If you have an IELTS certificate, you need to ensure it remains valid on the first day of your course.
limitations: RECENCY RULE with an explicit anchor: 'the first day of your course'. Third distinct anchor found in this batch (Bath: 'starting your course'; Edinburgh, previously: 'prior to entry'). A max-age constraint must carry its anchor or the arithmetic is wrong by up to a year.
researcher_notes: Stated for IELTS specifically, not for all tests.
